questions.text: Explain the administrative system of the Rashtrakutas.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the administrative system of the Rashtrakutas. (A)

answer.value:
Rashtrakuta Administration:
The Rashtrakutas followed a hereditary monarchy.
A council of ministers assisted the king.
The MahasandhiVigrahi handled foreign trade.
The empire was divided into mandalas, vishayas, nadus, and villages.
Village heads were called Gramapati or Prabhugavunda.
Nadu officials were known as Nadagavunda, and revenue came from land taxes, professional taxes, and foreign trade duties.

The MahasandhiVigrahi handled foreign trade.
The empire was divided into mandalas, vishayas, nadus, and villages.
Village heads were called Gramapati or Prabhugavunda.
Nadu officials were known as Nadagavunda, and revenue came from land taxes, professional taxes, and foreign trade duties.

questions.text: Explain the contributions of Kalyana Chalukyas in the field of literature
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the contributions of Kalyana Chalukyas in the field of literature (A)

answer.value:
Literature under Chalukyas of Kalyana:
Golden age of Kannada: The period of Kalyana Chalukyas is called the “Golden Age of Kannada Literature” because many great works were written.
Vachana Literature started: Social reformer Basavanna started the Vachana movement. Vachanas were simple poems in Kannada about God and society.
Great Kannada poets: Famous poets like Ranna, Pampa's followers, and Nagachandra wrote epics and stories that made Kannada literature rich.
Encouragement to Jain literature: Chalukya kings supported Jain scholars. Nagachandra wrote Ramachandra Charitapurana in Kannada.
Support to Sanskrit: Along with Kannada, Sanskrit also grew. Scholars wrote books on grammar, poetry, and science in Sanskrit.
New literary styles: New forms like Champu, Shatpadi, and Vachana became popular. Writing became easy for common people to understand.
Royal patronage: Kalyana Chalukya kings gave jobs, land, and rewards to poets and scholars. Their court at Kalyana was a center of learning.
Religious and social themes: Literature spoke about Bhakti, equality, and social reforms. This helped spread ideas to all people, not just scholars.

questions.text: Explain the achievements of Amoghavarsha.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the achievements of Amoghavarsha. (A)

answer.value:
Amoghavarsha ruled for about 64 years. This brought peace and stability to the Rashtrakuta kingdom.
Great administrator: He made good laws and had a strong, well-organized government. People lived safely.
Capital at Manyakheta: He made Manyakheta in present-day Karnataka his capital and developed it into a big city
Patron of literature: He loved Kannada and Sanskrit. He wrote “Kavirajamarga”, the first book on Kannada poetry.
Religious tolerance: Though he followed Jainism, he respected all religions. He built temples for Hindus and Jainas.
Support to arts and education: He encouraged poets, scholars, and artists. Many famous writers lived in his court.
Trade and economy: He promoted trade with Arab countries. Manyakheta became a rich center for business.
Peaceful ruler: Unlike other kings, he preferred peace over war. This helped culture, farming, and trade to grow.
Amoghavarsha is remembered as one of the greatest and most peaceful kings of India.

answer.value:
Rashtrakuta Period:
Patronage to Kannada: Made Kannada a court language. It became very popular during their rule.
Kavirajamarga: Written by King Amoghavarsha I. First book on Kannada grammar and poetry.
Three Gems of Kannada: Pampa, Ponna and Ranna wrote great Kannada epics under Rashtrakuta patronage.
Pampa's works: Wrote Adipurana and Pampa Bharata in champu style.
Jain literature grew: Most early Kannada works were Jain religious texts. Rashtrakutas supported Jain scholars.
Centers of learning: Manyakheta became a big center for poets, scholars, and libraries.
Great scholars in Amoghavarsha's court: His court had famous Jain scholars like Jinasena, Gunabhadra, Virasena, mathematician Mahaviracharya, and grammarian Shakatayana.
Kannada scholar - Srivijaya: He wrote Kavirajamarga in Amoghavarsha's court. It is the first available book on Kannada poetry.

questions.text: “The Rashtrakuta rulers were patrons of art.” Justify this statement with suitable examples.
questions.text_as_printed: “The Rashtrakuta rulers were patrons of art.” Justify this statement with suitable examples. (D)

answer.value:
The Rashtrakutas were great supporters of art and architecture during their rule from 8th to 10th century CE.
Ellora and Elephanta are great contributions to Indian art
Krishna I built the world-famous Kailasanatha Temple at Ellora by carving an entire mountain into a temple.
This temple shows their skill because it was made out of one single rock without joining any stones.
The Rashtrakutas also contributed to the Ellora caves and made beautiful sculptures of Shiva, Vishnu and Durga.
They encouraged rock-cut architecture and continued building temples in styles seen at Ellora and other places.
The idols of Ardhanarishvara and Maheshmurti (Trimukha) are beautifully carved. Temples from their period are found at Shiraval in Raichur district. There is also a beautiful Jain temple at Pattadakal.
The capital Manyakheta became a center where poets, painters and sculptors from different regions gathered.
Because of their royal support, art and culture reached great heights and is still admired today

answer.value:
Vikramaditya VI, the son of Someshvara I, was the greatest ruler of this dynasty.
An extraordinary warrior and a good administrator.
He started the Chalukya Vikrama era in 1076 CE.
He suppressed the rebellion of Hoysala Vishnuvardhana.
He maintained relations with Vijayabahu, the king of Sri Lanka.
